housing.summary: Delhi's rental market spans a wide range: central and expat-favoured areas like South Delhi (Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Defence Colony) and central New Delhi command high rents, while suburbs (Dwarka, Rohini) and NCR cities (Gurgaon/Gurugram, Noida) are more affordable. Furnished flats are common for expats. Deposits are typically 2-3 months' rent (higher for premium/independent houses). Brokers usually charge one month's rent as commission. Lease agreements are commonly 11 months to avoid rent-control registration.

banking.summary: Foreign nationals resident in India can open a resident savings account; non-residents use NRE/NRO accounts. Banks apply full KYC. Popular banks with expat services include HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI), Axis Bank, and international banks like Citibank, HSBC and Standard Chartered. A PAN card and valid visa/residence permit are generally required.

schools.summary: Delhi and the surrounding NCR host many international schools serving expat families, offering IB, British (IGCSE/A-level) and American curricula alongside the Indian CBSE and ICSE boards. Well-known options include The British School New Delhi, The American Embassy School, Pathways schools, and various IB World Schools. Admission is competitive and often requires advance application.

legal_admin.summary: Foreign nationals staying in India beyond 180 days on long-term visas (employment, student, research, etc.) must register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Delhi, generally within 14 days of arrival. Registration is done online via the e-FRRO portal and produces a Residential Permit. Address changes and visa extensions are also processed through FRRO/e-FRRO.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with the FRRO (Foreigners Regional Registration Office) via the e-FRRO portal within 14 days of arrival for long-term visas exceeding 180 days.

tax_finance.summary: India levies income tax administered by the Income Tax Department under the Central Board of Direct Taxes. Residency for tax purposes is determined by days of physical presence (the 182-day rule and related tests). Every taxpayer needs a Permanent Account Number (PAN); salaried employees have tax withheld at source (TDS). Foreign nationals should also assess tax-residency and any double-taxation treaty relief.

transport.summary: Delhi has an extensive public transport network anchored by the Delhi Metro (operated by DMRC), supplemented by DTC buses, autorickshaws, and app-based cabs (Uber/Ola). The Metro uses smart cards and QR tickets; a common mobility card is available. Traffic congestion is significant, so many expats rely on the Metro plus ride-hailing. Foreign licence holders can drive on an International Driving Permit short-term but should convert to an Indian licence for longer stays.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign nationals may drive on a valid foreign licence with an International Driving Permit for a limited period; for longer stays, apply to convert to / obtain an Indian driving licence via the Regional Transport Office (RTO) / Sarathi portal.
transport.healthcare_registration: India has no universal automatic health-registration for foreigners; expats typically rely on private health insurance and private hospitals. There is no national GP-registration equivalent, so arrange private medical insurance and identify preferred private hospitals/clinics.
